title: Static and dynamic assignment: DHCP, scopes and reservations

videos.script: Plug a laptop into an office network and it works within seconds. Nobody typed an address into it. {{plug}} Something lent it one, together with a gateway and a name server. That something is DHCP, and this lesson takes it apart. {{dhcp}} You will watch a PC with no address ask for one. Four messages go back and forth, and you will read all four, first from the client and then from the server's side of the cable. {{dora}} Then the server's file: the scope it lends from, how long a loan lasts, and a reservation that gives a printer the same address every time. {{config}} A lease is a loan with a date on it. You will read both records of one, and see when the client comes back to renew. {{leases}} A router stops broadcasts, so a second floor gets nothing, until the router relays its requests. {{relay}} And last, a second server that nobody asked for. You will see the network it breaks, and the switch rule that stops it. {{rogue}} Everything runs in this course's lab, on one Linux computer. So every line on the screen is what the machines really printed. {{lab}}
